_comment: Which pages of a design export get shipped, and under what name.
The export folder holds the same nine pages twice:
*.dc.html            loose source, 15-76 KB, no __bundler/manifest block.
Human-readable design source. Only dev/build-new-views.js
ever read these, and that script is retired (see below).
production/*.html    the bundled build, ~1.1 MB each, already named for
deployment. THIS is what build-live-pages.js reads --
it needs the manifest/template blocks the bundler emits.
So there is no rename to do: the design tool already emits deployed names.
What this file actually pins down is the ALLOW-LIST -- which bundled pages
ship. All ten of the 2026-08-03 (evening) export do: homesite.html joined as
the Homesite Detail page that JOB_LINK() resolves to, and tracker-new.html
-- the superseded 'New Views' prototype that used to need an ignore entry --
is gone from the export entirely. 'ignore' is empty as a result, and should
stay that way: an export that grows a page ought to stop the build and be a
decision, not an entry someone adds to make the error go away.
Keys are filenames inside production/. Values must match PAGES in
dev/build-live-pages.js exactly.
'ignore' is not a junk drawer -- each entry carries its reason, because an
unexplained entry is indistinguishable from a page someone forgot to wire.
